description.merchant: The {name} is {nationality} merchant sloop under the command of {captain}. Small, single-masted vessels like this are the backbone of trade between the islands of the Caribbean.
description.navy: The {name} is a sloop-of-war of the {navy} under the command of {captain}. Small, single-masted vessels like this are used for patrols, carrying dispatches, and sweeping for pirates.
description.privateer: The {name} is {nationality} sloop under the command of the privateer {captain}. These small, single-masted vessels are a favorite of small-syndicate privateering ventures because they’re fast, agile, and cheap to outfit.
description.pirate: The {name} is a pirate sloop under the command of {captain}. The small, single-masted vessels are considered the “perfect” pirate ships due to their speed, shallow draft, and maneuverability.

sloop.special: Can travel at full speed when Close to the Wind.

description.merchant: The {name} is {nationality} merchant brigantine under the command of {captain}. Square-rigged, two-masted vessels like this provide an excellent balance of speed and cargo capacity for trade.
description.navy: The {name} is a brigantine of the {navy} under the command of {captain}. These square-rigged, two-masted vessels are used for patrols, escorts, and carrying dispatches.
description.privateer: The {name} is a {nationality} sloop under the command of the privateer {captain}. These square-rigged, two-masted vessels are popular among privateering ventures for their balance of speed and deck space for more guns.
description.pirate: The {name} is a pirate brigantine under the command of {captain}. These square-rigged, two-masted vessels are favored by medium-sized crews that have outgrown a sloop.

fluyt.description: The {name} is a fluyt of the Dutch West India Company under the command of {captain}. These slow, high-sided merchant vessels are favored by the company for transporting cargo, troops, and treasure.

description.merchant: The {name} is {nationality} merchant frigate under the command of {captain}. A ship of this size must cross the Atlantic with some regularity, and be the prize of the company that owns it.
description.navy: The {name} is a frigate of the {navy} under the command of {captain}. Fast, well-armed ships like this are the navy’s standard cruising ship, used to escort important merchants, hunt pirates, and engage in battle.
description.privateer: The {name} is a {nationality} frigate under the command of the privateer {captain}. Only the largest, most well-funded privateering ventures could afford a ship like this.
description.pirate: The {name} is a pirate frigate under the command of {captain}. While not as nimble as a sloop, a fast ship like this makes a decent pirate flagship due to its size and armament.

manowar.description: The {name} is a warship of the {navy} under the command of {captain}. It is a large, heavily-armed vessel built for naval combat that requires a large, trained crew to operate. It is the power in these waters.

harpoon-gun.name: Harpoon Gun
harpoon-gun.special: Strength DR 12 or pulled to shooter

blunderbuss.name: Blunderbuss
blunderbuss.special: reload 2 actions, range 30', d10 damage under 10'

plate.name: Conquistador Plate
plate.special: DR +4 on Agility tests, defense is DR +2. You’ll most likely sink and drown in water

captain.core: Legendary Captain: While in command, the ship can take an extra crew action each round, even if it has already been taken.

options.a: Issue Command: The captain can take an action to give another member of the crew an action.
options.b: Aggressive Leader: Agility DR 14 to defend against the captain’s nearby allies’ attacks.
options.c: Careful Leader: DR 14 to attack the captain’s nearby allies.
options.d: Skilled Fighter: The captain attacks twice each round.

quartermaster.core: Veteran Quartermaster: While on board the ship, crew morale tests are +3. Cargo sells for 50% more in port.

options.a: Careful Leader: DR 14 to attack the quartermaster’s nearby allies.
options.b: Fences: Cargo sells for double in three specific ports (name them).
options.c: Trusted Advocate: The crew has a +1 bonus to morale while the quartermaster is in office.
options.d: Shipwrights: The quartermaster knows shipwrights in three specific ports (name them). {S} can arrange for 50% off repairs and upgrades, but what will they want in return?

quartermaster.description: {mister} is the veteran quartermaster of the {ship}.

bosun.core: Strict Bosun: While serving as bosun, once per combat the ship can reroll one Crew Action test.

options.a: To Arms, You Dogs: The bosun takes an action, DR 14 to defend against the bosun’s nearby allies for the next round.
options.b: Terrifying Presence: The bosun makes a threatening display. Nearby enemies must make a morale test.
options.c: Skilled Fighter: The bosun attacks twice each round.
options.d: Swearing Sailor: The bosun threatens an enemy {s} can see with an impressive display of coarse language. Test Spirit DR 14 or be stunned for the next round.

bosun.description: {mister} is the boatswain of the {ship}, known for running a tight ship.

gunner.core: Master Gunner: While serving as master gunner, ship attacks are -2 DR.

options.a: Black Powder Poet: The gunner has [[d4]] bombs, and is -2 DR when throwing them.
options.b: Reliable Gunner: The gunner does not fumble with black powder weapons.
options.c: Flintlock Fanatic: The gunner has three flintlock pistols and can attack with all of them in a single round. {S} can reload a pistol in a single round.
options.d: Old Broadsides: The gunner adds a +2 bonus to the broadsides action.

gunner.description: {mister} is the master gunner of the {ship}.

master.core: Master of Sails: While serving as sailing master, the ship’s Agility tests are -2 DR.

options.a: Speed Sailor: Adds +2 bonus to full sail action.
options.b: Nimble Sailor: Adds +2 bonus to come about action.
options.c: Extra Canvas: In naval combat, provides two additional actions: more canvas increases speed by +1 by adding +2 DR to the ship’s agility tests, less canvas restores the ship to its normal configuration.
options.d: Old Salt: The crew can sing an additional sea shanty per day.

master.description: {mister} is the sailing master aboard the {ship}.

sorcerer.core: Deck Sorcerer: Once per naval combat, change the speed and direction of the wind.

options.a: Wither: One creature the sorcerer can see tests Toughness DR 14 or takes [[/r d6]] damage.
options.b: Raise Dead: The sorcerer summons a skeletal thrall from a nearby corpse. It has 4 HP and bites or claws for [[/r d4]] damage. The skeleton obeys the sorcerer, but tumbles into lifeless bones at sunrise.
options.c: Ritualist: The sorcerer knows a random arcane ritual and can perform it once a day.
options.d: Familiar: The sorcerer has a familiar. {S} can speak with it, and it can report back to {o}.

sorcerer.description: {mister} is the deck sorcerer aboard the {ship}.

priest.core: Deck Priest: Once per naval combat, change the speed and direction of the wind.

options.a: Lay on Hands: Touch one creature to heal [[/r d4]] HP.
options.b: Holy Flame: A creature the priest can see tests Spirit DR 14 or takes [[/r d6]] damage.
options.c: Forbiddance: A creature the priest can see tests Spirit DR 14 or is stunned for one turn.
options.d: Religious Zeal: Agility DR 14 to defend against the priest’s nearby allies.

priest.description: {priest} is the deck priest aboard the {ship}.

carpenter.core: Master Carpenter: While serving as master carpenter, the ship’s repair actions are -5 DR.

options.a: Derelict Preserver: If the ship is derelict and take additional damage, roll twice and take the lower result.
options.b: Skilled Careener: After overseeing careening, the ship can sail for four months before taking penalties instead of three, and each day of careening accounts for 20 max HP rather than 10.
options.c: Effective Craftsman: Crew repairs recover 4 HP/day instead of 2.
options.d: Frugal Craftsman: Crew repairs cost 15s per HP instead of 25.

carpenter.description: {mister} is the master carpenter aboard the {ship}.
